title: Octopus Facts That Sound Fake
character_look: a purple cartoon octopus with big googly eyes, pink cheeks and a tiny yellow sailor cap
hook: An octopus has three hearts, and that's not even the weirdest part.

beats.narration: An octopus has three hearts, and that's not even the weirdest part.
beats.scene: Ollie juggling three heart-shaped balloons with two arms, eyes popping, sweating in panic.

beats.narration: Two hearts pump blood to the gills. The third pumps it to the rest of the body.
beats.scene: Ollie as a construction foreman blowing a whistle at two little hearts in hard hats marching toward a 'GILLS' sign, while a third heart heads to 'BODY'.

beats.narration: Their blood is blue, because it uses copper instead of iron to carry oxygen.
beats.scene: Ollie happily sipping a juice box labelled 'Cu' through a straw, dripping blue drops.

beats.narration: About two thirds of their neurons sit in their arms, so each arm can taste and react on its own.
beats.scene: Ollie at an underwater picnic, each arm holding a different snack: ice cream, a lollipop, cheese, as if every arm is tasting on its own.

beats.narration: And the weirdest part? When an octopus swims, the heart that feeds its body actually stops beating.
beats.scene: Ollie zooming through open water with dizzy spiral eyes while the heart on his belly naps in a bed, snoring 'Zzz'.

beats.narration: That's why they'd rather crawl. Which octopus fact surprised you most?
beats.scene: Ollie lounging in a striped deckchair next to a 'NO SWIM' sign, wearing a smug look, holding up a big question mark.

cta_question: Which octopus fact surprised you most?
description_body: Octopus facts that sound fake but are true: three hearts, blue copper-based blood, and arms packed with neurons.
pinned_comment: Three hearts or thinking arms: which is the more impressive superpower? 🐙
